question: Huawei is privately held and files nothing with the SEC. What revenue and net profit attributable to the parent company did Huawei publish for the first half of 2026 (six months ended June 30, 2026), how much did it spend on R&D (and what share of revenue is that), and what net profit margin does that imply? Note which profit figure you use, because two different 'net profit' numbers circulate.
grading: Key points (all required): (1) revenue RMB 467.82 billion, +9.55% (about +9.6%); (2) net profit attributable to the parent about RMB 23.43 billion (accept 23.4-23.5), down about 36.8% - OR, if the answer instead uses the Bloomberg headline net profit of RMB 23.81 billion (-36%), it must label that as the consolidated/headline figure; (3) R&D spending RMB 121.38 billion = about 25.9% of revenue (25.94%), up 25.2%; (4) implied net margin about 5.0% on the attributable figure (accept 4.9%-5.1%; 5.1% if 23.81 is used); (5) states that the figures are company-published, not SEC-filed. Optional: operating profit about RMB 32.77 billion (about 7.0% of revenue, one Chinese source). Fail if H1 2025 or full-year figures are used, if US dollars replace RMB, if net profit and its growth rate come from different definitions, or if the answer says Huawei filed with the SEC.
answer: H1 2026 (Jan-Jun, published 31 Aug 2026): revenue RMB 467.82bn (+9.55%); net profit attributable to the parent about RMB 23.43bn (-36.8%) - Bloomberg's RMB 23.81bn (-36%) is the headline/consolidated net profit; R&D RMB 121.38bn (+25.2%) = 25.9% of revenue; implied net margin about 5.0% (23.43/467.82; 5.1% on 23.81). Operating profit was about RMB 32.77bn (about 7.0%). These are Huawei's own published figures, not an SEC filing [W13-E1 to W13-E4].

output.answer:
Based on Huawei’s published interim results for the first half of 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026), reported in late August/early September 2026, here are the figures:

| Metric | H1 2026 |
|---|---|
| **Revenue** | **CNY 467.82 billion** (~USD 69.6–69.8 bn) |
| **R&D spending** | **CNY 121.38 billion** (~USD 18.1 bn) |
| **R&D as % of revenue** | **~25.9%** |
| **Net profit attributable to parent** | **CNY ~23.4 bn** (some sources cite CNY 23.81 bn) |
| **Net profit margin** (attributable) | **~5.0%** |

### Which profit figure to use
Two slightly different “net profit” numbers circulate:
- **CNY 23.4 billion** (attributable to parent-company shareholders, per WSJ, Yicai, and BigGo Finance) — down ~37% year-on-year. This is the **parent-attributable** number you asked for.
- **CNY 23.81 billion** (cited by Reuters, TelecomLead, Huawei Central, etc.) — down ~36% YoY. This appears to be the **consolidated “profit for the period”** (i.e., total net profit including a small non-controlling interest).

In Huawei’s IFRS reporting, the difference between consolidated net profit and profit attributable to equity holders of Huawei Investment & Holding is usually minor (e.g., in full-year 2024 it was CNY 62.57 bn vs. CNY 62.49 bn). I have therefore used **CNY ~23.4 billion** as the attributable figure.

### Implied net profit margin
Using the attributable profit figure:  
**CNY 23.4 bn ÷ CNY 467.82 bn ≈ 5.0%** (or ~5.1% if you use the CNY 23.81 bn consolidated figure).

### Context
The margin compression was deliberate: revenue grew 9.6% but R&D surged 25.2% as Huawei accelerated investment in AI, semiconductors, and automotive solutions under continued U.S. sanctions. Operating cash flow also turned negative (CNY –39.9 bn) due to higher component costs and supply-chain inventory build-up.

Sources: Reuters, WSJ, Yicai, TelecomLead, BigGo Finance, Huawei Central ([reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com), [wsj.com](https://www.wsj.com), [telecomlead.com](https://telecomlead.com), [startupfortune.com](https://startupfortune.com), [gulf-times.com](https://www.gulf-times.com)).
